programme: NR3C1 (glucocorticoid receptor), NR0B1 (DAX1), NR1I3 (CAR) and CREB1 form a corticosteroid/HPA-axis nuclear-receptor module: NR0B1 gates SF1-dependent adrenal steroidogenic genes including the ACTH receptor MC2R, CREB1 carries ACTH-cAMP-PKA signalling onto a gene set it shares with NR3C1 (PCK1, JUN, BCL2, PTGS2), and NR1I3 both targets NR3C1 directly and catabolizes glucocorticoids/xenobiotics downstream — together setting corticosteroid output, target-cell response, and clearance.
role_in_a: In Huntington's disease, HPA-axis hyperactivity with elevated, dysrhythmic cortisol is a documented non-motor feature that tracks with disease progression; mutant huntingtin also sequesters CBP away from CREB1, blunting CREB-dependent transcription of survival genes such as BCL2, so the same corticosteroid/cAMP module is hit both upstream (excess glucocorticoid drive) and downstream (impaired CREB1 output) in neurons.
role_in_b: In thymoma, glucocorticoid signalling through NR3C1 is the central pathway governing thymocyte apoptosis and positive/negative selection in the thymic microenvironment where these tumors arise, and disordered selection is mechanistically linked to the paraneoplastic autoimmunity (e.g. myasthenia gravis) that frequently accompanies thymoma; GR-driven regulation of BCL2/JUN-type apoptotic genes is the expected route.
shared_axis: Both diseases involve a specific cell population reading out systemic or local corticosteroid/cAMP signalling through the same receptor logic — striatal/cortical neurons in HD, developing thymocytes in thymoma — via an overlapping target gene set (PCK1, JUN, BCL2, PTGS2) co-regulated by NR3C1 and CREB1, with NR0B1-gated adrenal output and NR1I3-mediated catabolism setting how much hormone reaches either tissue.
reasoning: NR3C1 is independently placed in both diseases by strong Open Targets association scores (0.7461 in HD, 0.9751 in Thymoma), and the four factors form a textbook, nameable corticosteroid/cAMP nuclear-receptor circuit with internal cross-links (NR1I3 targets NR3C1; CREB1 and NR3C1 share PCK1/JUN/BCL2/PTGS2). But none of the reader's notes attach a PMID to NR0B1, NR3C1, NR1I3, or CREB1 in either disease, so the HD-thymoma connection rests on general endocrine/thymic physiology rather than retrieved literature, and none of these four sit among the top-recurring factors in this pair (69-74/210, ~33-35%, versus 82-84/210 for HDGF/MNX1/NFE2L2) — moderate, not strong.
support: none found for NR3C1, NR0B1, NR1I3, or CREB1; the record's only direct PMIDs for this pair (37580082 HDGF in HD, 42322611 TET1 in HD, 21179468 and 12736330 SP3 in HD) attach to factors outside this programme and were excluded from it because they don't extend to the nuclear-receptor/cAMP module.
how_to_falsify: Profile diurnal cortisol/ACTH together with NR3C1, NR0B1, NR1I3 and CREB1 occupancy/expression at PCK1, JUN, BCL2 and PTGS2 in matched HD striatal tissue or PBMCs versus thymoma tumor and peri-tumoral thymic tissue; absence of a coordinated HPA-axis transcriptional signature at these genes in either tissue, or a ChIP/reporter assay showing NR1I3 does not regulate NR3C1 and NR0B1/CREB1 do not co-regulate MC2R-driven output, would break the proposed mechanism.
caveats: Tissue pairing is blood|thymus; of the 210 patient-group comparisons only 2 are independent cohort pairs, so the denominator is inflated by combinatorial subgroupings within the same two cohorts rather than by independent replication. The tissue-generic exclusion list (SP1, RELB, RUNX3, NFKB2, STAT3, LITAF, EBF1, PRDM1, IRF7, CREB5, GFI1, E2F1) is entirely generic blood/immune TFs and does not overlap this nuclear-receptor module, so its absence there is not evidence for or against the account. The single-view list (ZNF32, SOX7, LHX9, MTA2, RUNX3, SKIL, ZNF287, TRERF1, PITX2, KLF2, ZNF135, MEF2C) contains no nuclear receptors, so this story is not an artifact of one patient subgroup. HDGF, TET1 and SP3 carry the only direct literature support in this pair but are HD-specific and were deliberately left out of the named programme rather than stretched to cover thymoma.
